root_cause.text: The fq_table[fq->idx] entry was not cleared before the FQID was returned to the memory pool via gen_pool_free(), allowing a concurrent thread to allocate the same FQID and trigger a WARN_ON when finding the stale fq_table entry still populated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch demonstrates the race condition where Thread A calls gen_pool_free() to release the FQID back to the pool, but Thread B can immediately allocate that same FQID via qman_alloc_fqid() before Thread A clears fq_table[fq->idx] = NULL. This causes Thread B's WARN_ON(fq_table[fq->idx]) check to fail because the table entry still references the old queue. The fix reorders operations to set fq_table[fq->idx] = NULL before calling gen_pool_free(), and uses smp_wmb() to ensure the write is visible to other CPUs before the FQID becomes available for reallocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix race condition in FQID release by reordering operations to clear fq_table before freeing the FQID, with memory barrier and leak detection.
intent_record.what: Replaced a simple qman_release_fqid() call with a multi-step sequence: (1) call qman_shutdown_fq() with leak detection, (2) set fq_table[fq->idx] to NULL, (3) add a memory barrier and conditional gen_pool_free() call. Added explanatory comments describing a race condition and the required ordering.
intent_record.how: This change fixes a race condition in FQID (Frame Queue ID) cleanup. Previously, the FQID was released before clearing the fq_table entry, creating a window where qman_alloc_fqid() could allocate the same FQID while fq_table still referenced it. The new sequence ensures fq_table is cleared first, uses a write memory barrier (smp_wmb) to enforce ordering, then safely frees the FQID. It also adds leak detection via qman_shutdown_fq() to warn if resources weren't properly released.
